text:
elena: heads up — running mypy against the latest py-sdk client surfaced a bunch of errors. looks like autogenerated models are typed as Dict[str, Any] / Any for response bodies.

sam: ugh yeah saw that in CI this morning. breakage in strict mode. do we have a plan to emit better types from the generator? :thinking_face: 

mike: the generator today is model-first but we only emit plain dataclasses with Any for nested fields. quick wins: generate TypedDicts or pydantic models instead of raw dicts.

jaya: pydantic would be nice for runtime validation but adds dep. could we emit .pyi stubs so users who opt-in to types get good hints without runtime change?

elena: i'd prefer minimal runtime impact. .pyi + py.typed in the package would fix mypy/pyright for most consumers. also need async typing for streaming endpoints — right now async client streaming uses `async def stream(...): yield` but the annotation is missing.

mike: agreed. for streaming we should annotate as -> AsyncIterator[bytes] or -> AsyncIterator[ModelChunk] depending on the response. current signature is `Any` so mypy loses track.

sam: can we sketch a change set: (1) add optional `--typed` flag to codegen that outputs typed models (TypedDict or dataclass generic types), (2) generate .pyi stubs for current output when not enabling pydantic, (3) annotate sync/async overloads and streaming return types.

jaya: +1 to the flag. devs can opt in until we decide default. also we should include types for client factory functions: `def Client(...)-> Client` is obvious but params should be typed (ApiKey | OAuth | None). many auth variants are untyped now.

elena: example errors from mypy CI:```
src/redwood_sdk/client.py:45: error: Function is missing a type annotation for one or more arguments  [no-untyped-def]
src/redwood_sdk/models/autogen.py:120: error: Incompatible types in assignment (expression has type "Dict[str, Any]", variable has type "TypedDict")
```

mike: hmm that second one looks like we attempted a TypedDict but codegen fell back to Dict[str, Any]. generator needs a deterministic mapping for optional/nullable fields -> Optional[T] vs Union[T, None].

sam: another angle: publish an official types package (redwood-sdk-types) that has only stubs and pydantic models. consumers who want strict typing can install it. avoids forcing runtime dep on pydantic for everyone.

jaya: that could work for enterprise where pinned deps are common. it adds maintenance overhead though.

elena: small UX bug I hit: VS Code/pyright doesn't pick up types unless py.typed is present in wheel. we must ensure packaging includes that file. also consider adding a typed stub resource for third-party type checkers.

mike: practical implementation plan I can take: 1) add .pyi stub gen step in build CI, 2) annotate all generated client functions with proper typing hints (including auth param union and RetryConfig typed dataclass), 3) add streaming async return annotations and overloads for sync vs async clients.

sam: do we have acceptance criteria? mypy strict pass for the SDK and example apps + pyright no errors in vscode workspace. also no regressions in runtime tests.

elena: yes. target: a PR that flips on stub generation in CI for a branch, then we can iterate. if we go with .pyi route first it's fastest.

dx-bot: CI report: mypy (strict) failed on branch feature/py-typing — 23 errors. see https://ci.redwood.example/12345

jaya: can someone attach a small reproducer? a minimal repo that imports the client and calls `client.chat.generate(...)` and runs mypy would speed debugging.

mike: i'll put up a small repro as a gist + a draft PR. plan to: commit stubgen script, add a `--emit-stubs` flag to codegen, and add packaging check for py.typed.

elena: thanks. one more item — docs: we should document typing story in the SDK README (how to opt-in, known limitations with streaming, recommended mypy config). that will reduce onboarding friction.

sam: +1. also we should surface this in the changelog and call out breaking typing changes in major releases.

jaya: ping @security if we add new auth union types so they review surface area? some teams rely on duck-typed auth objects.

mike: ack. i'll file a draft PR and post link here when ready. expected ETA: EOD Wed.

elena: great — leaving a checklist here: [ ] stubgen in CI, [ ] --emit-stubs flag, [ ] streaming annotations, [ ] py.typed in wheel, [ ] docs + sample mypy repo, [ ] security review.

sam: thanks team. :+1:
